chunk_findings.detail: The guard still does not tie `stale` to the confirmed fixes. If a gate is at its round cap and has one confirmed-and-fixed finding on `f1.py`, then after the fix an unrelated commit adds or changes `f2.py` (a file inside the same item), `stale` is non-empty because the current tree differs from the reviewed tree. With `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "untriaged": 0, "refuted": 0}`, the condition `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` is false, the stale protection is skipped, and `_settle_after_cap` settles the gate. The gate then passes over `f2.py` content no review ever saw. The bypass should require that the stale delta is exactly the confirmed fixes, not merely that no finding was refuted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:389

chunk_findings.detail: The stale-settle guard is still only `if stale and not counts.get("confirmed")`, not the claimed refined `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")`, and it does no path-level check that the stale movement is from the confirmed fix. Given a budget-capped gate where all findings are triaged and `counts` has at least one confirmed and at least one refuted, and after the round an unrelated commit changes a file covered by a refuted finding, `stale` is non-empty, `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, and the untriaged check below is false. Control therefore falls through to the mixed-set `passed_on_refutation` settle, passing a gate even though the refuted review is no longer against the tree the item holds now. Previous HIGH #1 still holds; this diff does not answer it.

chunk_findings.detail: The probe stated in the author’s triage (“if stale and (not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted"))”) does not answer the original finding. In the original scenario there is one confirmed finding, zero refutations, and an unrelated commit that moves the tree after the last review. Then `counts.get("refuted")` is 0 and `not counts.get("confirmed")` is False, so the stale protection is still skipped, and the gate passes even though the confirmed fix does not explain the current tree. No test added in this diff covers that case, so the HIGH finding still holds.

Given a gate with two findings where finding 1 is confirmed (moving `f1.py`) and an un-triaged or un-adjudicated third change or file `f3.py` is modified in the tree without a verdict, `counts.get("confirmed")` is true, which skips the stale tree check and prematurely permits the gate to settle or pass despite un-reviewed modifications outside the confirmed fix.

Given a gate at the round cap, all findings triaged, one confirmed finding on `f1.py`, one refuted finding on `f2.py`, and a later unrelated commit that changes `f2.py` after the reviewed snapshot, `stale` is non-empty and `counts["confirmed"]` is truthy, so line 394 does not return and the gate can record passed. chunk_findings.detail: `_movement_is_confirmed_fix` returns True whenever `moved is None` and any finding is confirmed, so `_settle_after_cap` skips the stale hold without evidence that the movement is the confirmed fix. In the worktree-disabled flow this change itself describes, `_moved_for` gets no `reviewed_paths` and passes `moved=None` into the settle used by `api.triage`. Given a cap-spent critic gate, finding 1 confirmed on `f1.py`, finding 2 refuted on `f2.py`, and a later edit to `f2.py` (or any other file) that makes `reviewed_other_tree` report that the item holds other content than the reviewed commit, `counts` is `{"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 1, "untriaged": 0}` and the gate still records `passed_on_refutation`. That is the mixed refuted-file move the new helper treats as not a confirmed fix (`_movement_is_confirmed_fix(..., ["f1.py", "f2.py"], ...)` is False), but the path `triage` actually calls never sees that list.

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only checks whether *any* finding is `confirmed`; it does not verify that the `stale` tree movement is the confirmed fix itself. Given a gate at budget cap with all findings triaged (`counts["untriaged"] == 0`), one confirmed finding (`counts["confirmed"] > 0`), and an unrelated commit that lands on the item after the last review, `stale` is non-empty because the current tree was not reviewed. Since `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, this line skips the stale protection, and the settle code below marks the gate passed even though the current tree contains unreviewed changes. The original guard existed precisely to prevent a pass when the reviewed tree is not the tree the item holds now.

chunk_findings.detail: The mixed test is vacuous for the boundary it claims to protect. `_setup` generates every finding on the same `x.py:{n}` line, and the confirmed fix changes exactly that line (`x = 2  # fixed finding 1`). So the moved content for the refuted finding is the very text explained by the confirmed fix. An implementation of `_settle_after_cap` that merely checks “there is at least one confirmed finding, so ignore the stale tree for every refutation” would pass this test, even though it would incorrectly pass a gate when a refuted finding is on a different moved file/line whose change no confirmed fix explains. A correct regression test must move a file/line for the refuted finding independently of the confirmed fix and assert the gate still fails.

chunk_findings.detail: `counts.get("confirmed")` checks for the existence of *any* confirmed finding in the current round, but does not verify whether all findings from that stale round have been triaged. If a round produces multiple findings and only a subset are triaged as `confirmed` while others remain untriaged or are in different states, `counts.get("confirmed")` evaluates to truthy and bypasses the stale check, allowing a gate to settle prematurely before all findings are resolved.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard still only inspects verdict counts, so it cannot tell whether the stale tree movement is the confirmed fix or an unrelated change. Given `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 0, "untriaged": 0}` and an unrelated commit landing on the item after the last reviewed tree, `stale` is non-empty. The condition `(not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted"))` is false, so the stale block is skipped; `counts.get("untriaged", 1)` is 0, so execution proceeds to the all-confirmed settle path. The gate can pass without any round having reviewed the current tree.

chunk_findings.detail: The test docstring now locks in “A stale tree still blocks a pass as soon as any finding was REFUTED,” and the added mixed test (`test_a_refutation_still_blocks_over_a_moved_tree_even_mixed_with_a_confirmed_fix`) has a refuted finding on an untouched f2.py while the confirmed fix moved only f1.py, but asserts the gate stays failed. That is the buggy mixed scenario from B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path (12 refuted, 7 confirmed-and-fixed): once f1.py’s movement is accounted for as the confirmed fix, the gate should settle with `passed_on_refutation` false, not stay failed. If the intended `_filtered_moved` implementation filters that confirmed-fix path, this test fails; if the test’s expected failure is enforced, the bug remains for any mixed refuted+confirmed round.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten test now asserts the gate remains `"failed"` after the review budget is spent, with finding 1 confirmed and its fix moving f1.py, and finding 2 refuted on an untouched file. This is the situation the change is meant to resolve: the intent says the gate must not stay failed after mixed confirmed-and-fixed plus refuted findings once the budget is spent, and the removed test previously asserted `outcome == "passed"`. By expecting failure, this regression test will fail on a correct fix path and lock in B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path instead of fixing it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_settle_after_cap` evaluates `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` on line 394 to determine whether to block a gate outcome due to a stale tree. However, `counts` is a dictionary of finding counts by verdict (e.g. `{"confirmed": n, "refuted": m}`), and `counts.get("refuted")` returns an integer count, not a boolean. If a round has `counts["refuted"] = 0`, `counts.get("refuted")` evaluates to the integer `0`, which is falsy in Python. But if `counts["refuted"]` is a positive integer (e.g., `1`), `counts.get("refuted")` evaluates to `1`, which is truthy. Consequently, when `counts["refuted"]` is zero, `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` depends solely on `not counts.get("confirmed")`, which correctly guards all-confirmed sets. But when `counts["refuted"]` is non-zero, the expression evaluates to `not counts.get("confirmed") or 1`, which evaluates to `True` regardless of whether `counts.get("confirmed")` is true or false. Thus, any gate with at least one refuted finding will *always* trigger the stale check and fail to settle, even if it also has confirmed findings or if no stale check was intended. For example, given a gate at budget cap with 1 confirmed finding and 1 refuted finding (`counts = {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 1}`), `not counts.get("confirmed")` is `False`, but `counts.get("refuted")` is `1` (truthy), so `False or 1` yields `True`, incorrectly blocking the mixed-fix/refutation scenario that the author attempted to permit or handle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The new predicate still refuses the exact triage the bug names. With the round budget spent, a non-empty `stale` message, and counts `{confirmed: 7, refuted: 12, untriaged: 0}` (the rubber_duck case: every finding triaged, the tree moved only because the confirmed fixes landed), `counts.get("refuted")` is truthy, so this line returns `{gate} stays failed: {stale}` and never reaches the settle that should record passed on refutation. The previous comment on this branch said a mixed set settles `on-refutation`; replacing `not counts.get("confirmed")` with `not confirmed or refuted` drops that path and only lets an all-confirmed round through. The critic-gate outcome cited in the bug (same triage, passed on refutation) cannot happen here whenever any refutation is present and the fix commit moved the tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The regression oracle contradicts the bug it claims to close. B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path is the mixed triage: 12 refuted and 7 confirmed-and-fixed, tree moved only by those fixes, gate stuck on "holds other content" while the same triage passed on refutation. This test sets that input up (finding 1 confirmed by rewriting only f1.py, finding 2 refuted on untouched f2.py) and then requires `passed_on_refutation is False`, gate outcome `failed`, and `"holds other content"` in the text. A correct settle would record passed on refutation once the only movement is the confirmed fix; this assertion forces the implementation to keep the no-fix-path for every mixed round, so the reported ADP-census-v2 case still cannot flip the gate.

chunk_findings.detail: The new stale guard `if stale and not counts.get("confirmed")` still lets a mixed gate settle over content the gate never reviewed when any finding is confirmed, without verifying that the confirmed fix is what moved the tree. Input: budget is spent, the last round has counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 1, untriaged: 0}`, and an unrelated commit lands on the item after that review. `stale` is non-empty because the reviewed tree is not the current tree, but `not counts.get("confirmed")` is `False`, so the stale block is skipped and the mixed settle below records `passed_on_refutation`/passes the gate over the unrelated change. The removed `or counts.get("refuted")` previously blocked this mixed-stale case; the new condition deletes that protection without adding any check that the tree movement is attributable to the confirmed fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten stale guard is only `if stale and not counts.get("confirmed")`, so any positive confirmed count skips the block even when the movement is not that fix. With the round budget spent, `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 1, "untriaged": 0}`, and a later commit that changes the file the refuted finding said was fine (or any path the confirmed fix did not touch), `stale` is non-empty because the current tree was not reviewed. `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, so this line does not return `{gate} stays failed: {stale}` and the settle below records `passed` / `passed_on_refutation`. That is wrong under the comment’s own B835d22b138 rule: a refutation is only valid for the tree that was reviewed, and a confirmed fix does not make unrelated content reviewed.

chunk_findings.detail: When the recorded round has no `reviewed_paths`, `_moved_for` yields `None` and this helper returns `True` as soon as `counts["confirmed"]` is non-zero, so the stale guard in `_settle_after_cap` is skipped. That is the worktree-disabled path the new test itself documents (`_setup` records no `reviewed_paths`, end-to-end settle keeps `moved=None`). Input: budget spent, counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 1, untriaged: 0}`, finding 1 fixed only in `f1.py`, and `f2.py` (the refuted finding’s file) also changed after the reviewed tree. `moved is None`, the helper returns `True`, and the gate settles passed-on-refutation over content the round never reviewed.

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate treats any path subset of historical confirmed locations as “the fix”, without comparing content to the reviewed tree. Input: budget spent, one confirmed finding whose location is `f1.py`, counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 0, untriaged: 0}`, and a later commit that changes `f1.py` again (or replaces the fix with different content) so the current blob is not what the round saw. `moved == ["f1.py"]`, `set(moved) - {"f1.py"}` is empty, the helper returns `True`, and `_settle_after_cap` records a pass on a tree the gate never reviewed. The same hole applies if an older confirmed finding cited `f1.py` and this round’s movement is a new edit to that file.

An implementation of `_settle_after_cap` that merely checks “there is at least one confirmed finding, so ignore the stale tree for every refutation” would pass this test, even though it would incorrectly pass a gate when a refuted finding is on a different moved file/line whose change no confirmed fix explains. A correct regression test must move a file/line for the refuted finding independently of the confirmed fix and assert the gate still fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py: test_mixed_refuted_and_confirmed_settle_despite_the_fix_moving_the_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `counts.get("confirmed")` checks for the existence of *any* confirmed finding in the current round, but does not verify whether all findings from that stale round have been triaged. If a round produces multiple findings and only a subset are triaged as `confirmed` while others remain untriaged or are in different states, `counts.get("confirmed")` evaluates to truthy and bypasses the stale check, allowing a gate to settle prematurely before all findings are resolved.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:389

chunk_findings.detail: The guard still only inspects verdict counts, so it cannot tell whether the stale tree movement is the confirmed fix or an unrelated change. Given `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 0, "untriaged": 0}` and an unrelated commit landing on the item after the last reviewed tree, `stale` is non-empty. The condition `(not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted"))` is false, so the stale block is skipped; `counts.get("untriaged", 1)` is 0, so execution proceeds to the all-confirmed settle path. The gate can pass without any round having reviewed the current tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The test docstring now locks in “A stale tree still blocks a pass as soon as any finding was REFUTED,” and the added mixed test (`test_a_refutation_still_blocks_over_a_moved_tree_even_mixed_with_a_confirmed_fix`) has a refuted finding on an untouched f2.py while the confirmed fix moved only f1.py, but asserts the gate stays failed. That is the buggy mixed scenario from B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path (12 refuted, 7 confirmed-and-fixed): once f1.py’s movement is accounted for as the confirmed fix, the gate should settle with `passed_on_refutation` false, not stay failed. If the intended `_filtered_moved` implementation filters that confirmed-fix path, this test fails; if the test’s expected failure is enforced, the bug remains for any mixed refuted+confirmed round.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py:8

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten test now asserts the gate remains `"failed"` after the review budget is spent, with finding 1 confirmed and its fix moving f1.py, and finding 2 refuted on an untouched file. This is the situation the change is meant to resolve: the intent says the gate must not stay failed after mixed confirmed-and-fixed plus refuted findings once the budget is spent, and the removed test previously asserted `outcome == "passed"`. By expecting failure, this regression test will fail on a correct fix path and lock in B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path instead of fixing it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py: test_a_refutation_still_blocks_over_a_moved_tree_even_mixed_with_a_confirmed_fix

chunk_findings.detail: `_settle_after_cap` evaluates `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` on line 394 to determine whether to block a gate outcome due to a stale tree. However, `counts` is a dictionary of finding counts by verdict (e.g. `{"confirmed": n, "refuted": m}`), and `counts.get("refuted")` returns an integer count, not a boolean. If a round has `counts["refuted"] = 0`, `counts.get("refuted")` evaluates to the integer `0`, which is falsy in Python. But if `counts["refuted"]` is a positive integer (e.g., `1`), `counts.get("refuted")` evaluates to `1`, which is truthy. Consequently, when `counts["refuted"]` is zero, `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` depends solely on `not counts.get("confirmed")`, which correctly guards all-confirmed sets. But when `counts["refuted"]` is non-zero, the expression evaluates to `not counts.get("confirmed") or 1`, which evaluates to `True` regardless of whether `counts.get("confirmed")` is true or false. Thus, any gate with at least one refuted finding will *always* trigger the stale check and fail to settle, even if it also has confirmed findings or if no stale check was intended. For example, given a gate at budget cap with 1 confirmed finding and 1 refuted finding (`counts = {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 1}`), `not counts.get("confirmed")` is `False`, but `counts.get("refuted")` is `1` (truthy), so `False or 1` yields `True`, incorrectly blocking the mixed-fix/refutation scenario that the author attempted to permit or handle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The new predicate still refuses the exact triage the bug names. With the round budget spent, a non-empty `stale` message, and counts `{confirmed: 7, refuted: 12, untriaged: 0}` (the rubber_duck case: every finding triaged, the tree moved only because the confirmed fixes landed), `counts.get("refuted")` is truthy, so this line returns `{gate} stays failed: {stale}` and never reaches the settle that should record passed on refutation. The previous comment on this branch said a mixed set settles `on-refutation`; replacing `not counts.get("confirmed")` with `not confirmed or refuted` drops that path and only lets an all-confirmed round through. The critic-gate outcome cited in the bug (same triage, passed on refutation) cannot happen here whenever any refutation is present and the fix commit moved the tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The regression oracle contradicts the bug it claims to close. B-review-round-budget-no-fix-path is the mixed triage: 12 refuted and 7 confirmed-and-fixed, tree moved only by those fixes, gate stuck on "holds other content" while the same triage passed on refutation. This test sets that input up (finding 1 confirmed by rewriting only f1.py, finding 2 refuted on untouched f2.py) and then requires `passed_on_refutation is False`, gate outcome `failed`, and `"holds other content"` in the text. A correct settle would record passed on refutation once the only movement is the confirmed fix; this assertion forces the implementation to keep the no-fix-path for every mixed round, so the reported ADP-census-v2 case still cannot flip the gate.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py:test_a_refutation_still_blocks_over_a_moved_tree_even_mixed_with_a_confirmed_fix

chunk_findings.detail: The new stale guard `if stale and not counts.get("confirmed")` still lets a mixed gate settle over content the gate never reviewed when any finding is confirmed, without verifying that the confirmed fix is what moved the tree. Input: budget is spent, the last round has counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 1, untriaged: 0}`, and an unrelated commit lands on the item after that review. `stale` is non-empty because the reviewed tree is not the current tree, but `not counts.get("confirmed")` is `False`, so the stale block is skipped and the mixed settle below records `passed_on_refutation`/passes the gate over the unrelated change. The removed `or counts.get("refuted")` previously blocked this mixed-stale case; the new condition deletes that protection without adding any check that the tree movement is attributable to the confirmed fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten stale guard is only `if stale and not counts.get("confirmed")`, so any positive confirmed count skips the block even when the movement is not that fix. With the round budget spent, `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "refuted": 1, "untriaged": 0}`, and a later commit that changes the file the refuted finding said was fine (or any path the confirmed fix did not touch), `stale` is non-empty because the current tree was not reviewed. `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, so this line does not return `{gate} stays failed: {stale}` and the settle below records `passed` / `passed_on_refutation`. That is wrong under the comment’s own B835d22b138 rule: a refutation is only valid for the tree that was reviewed, and a confirmed fix does not make unrelated content reviewed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:394

chunk_findings.detail: When the recorded round has no `reviewed_paths`, `_moved_for` yields `None` and this helper returns `True` as soon as `counts["confirmed"]` is non-zero, so the stale guard in `_settle_after_cap` is skipped. That is the worktree-disabled path the new test itself documents (`_setup` records no `reviewed_paths`, end-to-end settle keeps `moved=None`). Input: budget spent, counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 1, untriaged: 0}`, finding 1 fixed only in `f1.py`, and `f2.py` (the refuted finding’s file) also changed after the reviewed tree. `moved is None`, the helper returns `True`, and the gate settles passed-on-refutation over content the round never reviewed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_movement_is_confirmed_fix

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate treats any path subset of historical confirmed locations as “the fix”, without comparing content to the reviewed tree. Input: budget spent, one confirmed finding whose location is `f1.py`, counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 0, untriaged: 0}`, and a later commit that changes `f1.py` again (or replaces the fix with different content) so the current blob is not what the round saw. `moved == ["f1.py"]`, `set(moved) - {"f1.py"}` is empty, the helper returns `True`, and `_settle_after_cap` records a pass on a tree the gate never reviewed. The same hole applies if an older confirmed finding cited `f1.py` and this round’s movement is a new edit to that file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_movement_is_confirmed_fix

chunk_findings.detail: The stale relax still treats “moved paths ⊆ confirmed finding locations” as proof the unreviewed tree is the fix, with no blob check and no limit to this round’s fixes. At a spent budget (`used >= cap`), counts `{confirmed: 1, refuted: 1, untriaged: 0}`, a confirmed location `f1.py`, and a later edit that changes `f1.py` again (or any other file already cited by a historical confirmed verdict in `it.triage[gate]`), `_filtered_moved` returns those paths, `set(moved) - confirmed` is empty, and the helper returns True. Line `if stale and not _movement_is_confirmed_fix(...)` then skips the stale block and the settle records passed-on-refutation. The probe that a later commit is “a new delta a re-review reads” is false here: once `used >= cap` this function settles instead of requesting a round, and `rec.outcome == "passed"` keeps later calls from reopening it. The gate therefore passes on content the round never saw.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `effect` on `lessons.test_file_globs` states a behavior the entry does not have. Given the 0.2.6 change (old root-only `tests/**`/`test/**` plus Python name globs, new `**/spec/**`, `**/specs/**`, `**/__tests__/**`, and JS/TS/Go/Ruby name globs), the effect claims a bug whose fix is only in those files "is now verified against it instead of being treated as code to review." The key and the completed `why` on the previous line only define which paths name TEST files for lessons; they say nothing about bug verification or skipping review. An upgrade reader of 0.2.6 therefore acts on a policy change this knob does not record.
